note: INTENTIONAL, DOCUMENTED GAP (not a bug): create_user()/update_user() read `data = request.get_json()` then access `data['email']`/`data['username']` on the local variable (lines 54, 77). Stage A's Flask rule only matches request.form/json/args[...] subscripts and .get(...) calls directly on the `request` object, not a get_json() result reassigned to a variable. Real PII collection, currently undetected. Kept in ground truth so the gap stays visible in recall rather than silently disappearing.
Same get_json()-into-local-variable gap as above — data['username'] (lines 51, 73), classified under the lexicon's generic "name" bucket.

INTENTIONAL, DOCUMENTED GAP (not a bug): User.from_dict() reads `data['password']` (line 257) and hashes it via set_password() — the actual password-field access lives here, one call removed from the request.get_json() call site in users.py, since from_dict() is a shared model method called with the already-extracted dict. Same get_json()-into-variable detection boundary as the email/username gap above; no cross-function data-flow tracing today.
